AUTHOR: Silva-Alvarado
TITLE: Development of a Novel Convolution to Interactive Capture and Recalibration Enhancement Module for Underwater Fish Detection in Sensor Networks
SPECIES: blue whiting, herring, mackerel, mesopelagic group
DATA: Fish_YOLO_Dataset (authors' Zenodo; 'Synthetic and Real Underwater Image Dataset'), images from oceanographic campaigns
V_EV: Sec 3.1: 'two distinct lighting profiles captured across different oceanographic campaigns and highly variable water turbidity levels'
D_EV: Sec 3.1: 'The dataset partition consists of 5652 images for Training, 309 images for Validation, and 918 images for Testing' (unit not stated)
R_EV: Sec 5.4: 'experiments were conducted on a single Northeast Atlantic dataset; generalization to other marine ecosystems ... remains to be tested'
C_EV: Sec 4.3: 'Solving for Δ(θ) → 0 yielded an analytical optimal threshold of θopt = 0.327'
E_EV: Sec 4.3: 'the model achieved an R2count of 0.8846 and an MAE of 0.419 ± 1.494' (predicted vs ground-truth counts per frame)
ARCH: YOLO26n + C2ICARE attention module (also YOLO variants)
METR: P, R, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, count bias/MAE/MAPE/R2, FPS/GFLOPs
NOTE: Eligibility uncertain: dataset title says 'Synthetic and Real'; species/resolution (1392x1040) and ref to Allken et al. suggest Deep Vision in-trawl camera imagery, but the paper never states the platform or whether test images are real. Included on 'oceanographic campaigns' field provenance. Threshold optimised on validation set by count-discrepancy regression. Count reference = ground-truth annotations of same frames.
